name: The Gnarled Lime of Hallerwiese
access: Free, public city park (Hallerwiese, St. Johannis district)
transport: Short walk (roughly 15-20 min) from Nuremberg Altstadt/Hauptmarkt; specific tram/bus stop not verified this pass
verify_notes: Official Naturdenkmal ND-5 (register id ND-04981), St. Johannis Flur 4, tree-level GPS from Bayern's Naturdenkmale open-data layer. Nordbayern.de's survey of Nuremberg's oldest trees independently describes this as a gnarled linden roughly 350+ years old in the south of Hallerwiese, damaged by lightning and storm but still growing. Species is genus-only: no source specifies Sommerlinde (Tilia platyphyllos) vs Winterlinde (Tilia cordata) vs the common hybrid (Tilia x europaea) for THIS specific tree, so do not sharpen beyond 'lime'. Behind this tree, per the same article, stand two large plane trees planted around the same time, 300+ years old - see nbg_002 and nbg_003.

name: The Chestnut of Kontumazgarten
access: Free, public city park (Kontumazgarten, Kleinweidenmühle district), has a playground
transport: Short walk (roughly 15-20 min) from Nuremberg Altstadt/Hauptmarkt; specific tram/bus stop not verified this pass
verify_notes: Official Naturdenkmal ND-6 (register id ND-05043), Kleinweidenmühle Flur 137. Single-sourced beyond the register/ordinance: no independent article names this specific tree. Species recorded only as 'Kastanie' in the ordinance; the German default for an unqualified 'Kastanie' in a planted municipal park is Rosskastanie (Aesculus hippocastanum, horse chestnut) rather than Esskastanie (sweet chestnut), and Wikipedia's Kontumazgarten coverage discusses Rosskastanie in the same park, but no source names THIS tree specifically, so species is inferred, not confirmed - flag. IMPORTANT CAVEAT: during 2017 renovation works in this same park, a field maple and a Rosskastanie were felled due to trunk damage. This ND-6 chestnut still appears on the city's own 2020 official Naturdenkmal ordinance, three years after that felling, which is evidence it is a different, surviving tree rather than the one removed, but a writer or future pass should treat this as worth a fresh confirmation of life rather than settled fact.

name: The Old Lime of Stadtpark

location.address: Stadtpark, northeast of the Stadtparkweiher pond, south of the Schiller monument

transport: 'Stadtpark' bus stop (line N1); roughly 15-20 min walk from Nuremberg Hauptbahnhof
verify_notes: Official Naturdenkmal ND-38 (register id ND-05064), Gärten bei Wöhrd Flur 184. Best-evidenced tree of this batch: nordbayern.de's survey of Nuremberg's oldest trees calls it one of the city's strongest and oldest, roughly 400 years old with a trunk circumference of about 8 metres, opposite the Schiller monument. baumkunde.de (independent German tree database, verification use only per house rules) carries a dedicated entry for this exact tree and assessed it botanically as most likely a Sommerlinde (Tilia platyphyllos, Large-leaved Lime) based on leaf hairiness, though a sign at the tree itself reads 'Winterlinde' (Tilia cordata) - a genuine dispute between the physical signage and an independent leaf-based ID, flagged rather than picking a winner silently; the story could mention both. One of the strongest 'worth the walk' candidates in this whole batch for its age, girth and dedicated sourcing.
